fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Front Driveway; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure; Open Terrain; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the entry point and improve visibility at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Identify and designate a flat, open area on the property where emergency vehicles can turn around, and keep that area clear of equipment, vehicles, and debris at all times.
• Keep the full width of the driveway clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and overhanging vegetation so emergency vehicles can travel its full length without obstruction.
• Post the property address visibly at the driveway entrance rather than only at the residence, so responders do not have to travel the full length of the driveway before confirming they have the correct property.
• Trim any vegetation along the driveway edges that narrows the travel width or reduces clearance for larger emergency vehicles.
• Keep the area in front of the detached structure accessible so responders can reach it without repositioning vehicles.
• Confirm that perimeter gates, if any are present along the driveway, can be opened quickly from the outside and are not secured with locks unfamiliar to responders.
• Consider providing a Knox Box or coded gate access at the driveway entrance if any gate restricts emergency vehicle entry.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Long Driveway; Vegetation Along Driveway; Grass Cover; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Terrain; Scattered Shrubs; Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches and shrubs that overhang or touch the sides of the structure.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Cut grass close to the structure and keep it short throughout the dry season.
• Thin scattered shrubs near the structure to increase open space between individual plants.
• Clear dead grass and plant material from the ground around the base of the structure.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway so vehicles and emergency equipment can pass through without obstruction.
• Cut back shrubs and tall grass growing along the driveway edges to keep the travel path clear.
• Remove any dead or dry plant material that has accumulated along the driveway corridor.
• Keep grass along the driveway mowed short to reduce dry material between plants and the travel surface.
